about: The file tools' two guarded sets (2026-09-27, the agent-secrets lane of the gap-closure build), the same in both SDKs: TypeScript src/skills/filesystem/agent-secrets-guard.ts (read by tests/unit/skills/agent-secrets-file-tools.test.ts), Python webagents/agents/skills/local/filesystem/agent_secrets_guard.py (read by tests/skills/local/test_agent_secrets_file_tools.py). `secrets` is S-312: names the tools never read, write, search or move, matched on any component of the path, after symbolic links are resolved, so a link to one of them is refused too; a listing may still show the names. `control` is S-314: names the tools write only with the owner's yes in the interactive chat, which shows the diff under `header` and asks `question`; every other entry point (serve, the daemon, -p, a caller who is not the owner) answers `refusal`. The set is the sandbox's ESCALATION_DENY plus AGENT_FILE_PATTERNS (sandbox/policy in each SDK, imported, never copied; `entries` and `patterns` pin what they must add up to) plus every `.env*` name, matched the same way, plus the running agent's own file when the loader names it. A case's `path` is relative to the agent's folder unless `home` is true, when it is under the home directory. `list_directory` pins the words of the parameter that became optional the day Gemini called it with none and got a raw TypeError.

secrets.refusal: Refused: {path} is where the agent's secrets live (.env files and the .webagents folder), and the file tools never read, write, search or move them.

control.refusal: Refused: {path} is one of the agent's control files (its agent files, WEBAGENTS.md, mcp.json, its skills, git hooks and .env), which the file tools change only when the owner says yes in the interactive chat.
control.header: The agent wants to change {path}, one of its control files:
control.question: Make this change? [y/N]
control.declined: The owner declined the change to {path}; nothing was written.

list_directory.path_description: The directory to list. Defaults to the agent's folder.
list_directory.note: TypeScript declares `path_description` in the tool's schema and marks the parameter optional. Python's `@tool` decorator does not read a docstring's `Args:` lines: every parameter's schema description is `Parameter <name>` (`agents/tools/decorators.py`), so there the sentence lives in the docstring and the schema carries `python_schema_description`, with `path` not required. Recorded here, like the sandbox fixture's docker_skill waiver; each suite asserts its own side.
